For, 18 : 24

⇒ 6 + 18 = 24.

Similarly, for ? : 28

• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**

questions.question: Why are the intermediate goods NOT included in the National Income?

options.text: For the prevention of double accounting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**For the prevention of double accounting.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Intermediate goods** are not included in the National Income to prevent double accounting.
 
• Including intermediate goods would lead to **double counting** because their value is already embedded in the final goods and services.
 
• National Income is a measure of the total value of **final goods and services** produced in an economy over a specific period.
 
• Counting intermediate goods separately would **inflate the National Income** figures inaccurately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Intermediate goods are those goods that are used as inputs to produce other goods and services.
 
• Examples of intermediate goods include raw materials, components, and parts used in manufacturing.
 
• Final goods are those that are ready for consumption or investment and are included in the calculation of National Income.
 
• To accurately measure the economic activity and avoid overestimation, only the value of final goods and services is counted.

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at 60 km/h and 42 km/h. The faster train crosses a man in the slower train in 36 seconds. Find the length of the faster train.

questions.question: If the polynomial (2x³ + ax² + 3x - 5) and (x³ + x² - 2x + a) leave the same remainder when divided by (x-2), find the remainder.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By **Remainder Theorem**, equate **P(2)** and **Q(2)** because they leave the same remainder when divided by (x − 2).

2(2)³ + a(2)² + 3(2) − 5 = (2)³ + (2)² − 2(2) + a

16 + 4a + 6 − 5 = 8 + 4 − 4 + a ⇒ 17 + 4a = 8 + a

3a = −9 ⇒ a = −3

Substitute a = −3 in Q(2): Remainder = 8 + (−3) = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Polynomial** P(x) = 2x³ + ax² + 3x − 5

**Polynomial** Q(x) = x³ + x² − 2x + a

**Divisor** = (x − 2)

According to the **Remainder Theorem**, when a polynomial f(x) is divided by (x − c), the **remainder** is f(c).

Here, c = 2. Let the remainders be R₁ and R₂.

⇒ R₁ = P(2) = 2(2)³ + a(2)² + 3(2) − 5

⇒ R₁ = 2(8) + 4a + 6 − 5 = 16 + 4a + 1 = 17 + 4a

⇒ R₂ = Q(2) = (2)³ + (2)² − 2(2) + a

⇒ R₂ = 8 + 4 − 4 + a = 8 + a

Since the problem states both polynomials leave the **same remainder**:

⇒ R₁ = R₂

⇒ 17 + 4a = 8 + a

⇒ 4a − a = 8 − 17

⇒ 3a = −9

⇒ a = −3

Now, find the **actual remainder** by substituting a = −3 into either R₁ or R₂:

⇒ Remainder = 8 + a = 8 + (−3) = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Remainder Theorem

If a **polynomial** f(x) is divided by (x − a), the **remainder** is simply the value of the polynomial at x = a, denoted as f(a).

Factor Theorem

A special case of the remainder theorem where if f(a) = 0, then (x − a) is a **factor** of the polynomial f(x).

Division Algorithm

For any polynomials p(x) and g(x), there exist unique polynomials q(x) and r(x) such that p(x) = g(x) × q(x) + r(x), where **degree** of r(x) < degree of g(x).</p
